quiz.title: Addition of Matrices Quiz — Class 10 ICSE
quiz.intro: Eight questions on adding matrices at ICSE Class 10 level: order, when addition is allowed, 2×2 sums, the zero matrix and commutativity. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Addition of matrices for Class 10 ICSE

questions.q: Two matrices can be added only when
options: they have the same number of rows only
questions.explanation: Addition is defined only for matrices of the same order — the same number of rows AND the same number of columns — because you add corresponding elements.

questions.q: A is a 2×3 matrix and B is a 3×2 matrix. Is A + B possible?
questions.explanation: A is 2×3 and B is 3×2, so their orders do not match. Addition is not defined, even though multiplication AB would be.

questions.q: The additive identity for 2×2 matrices is
questions.explanation: Adding the zero (null) matrix leaves any matrix unchanged: A + O = A. The identity matrix I is the identity for multiplication, not addition.

questions.q: For matrices of the same order, A + B is equal to
questions.explanation: Matrix addition is commutative: A + B = B + A, because each pair of corresponding elements is added and ordinary number addition is commutative.

questions.q: If A = [[4, 0], [1, 3]], then A + O, where O is the 2×2 zero matrix, is
questions.explanation: O is the additive identity, so A + O = A. Nothing changes: the answer is [[4, 0], [1, 3]].
First multiply by the scalar: 2A = [[2, 4], [6, 8]]. Then add B: 2+0=2, 4+1=5, 6+2=8, 8+0=8, giving [[2, 5], [8, 8]].
Subtract A from both sides: B = (A + B) − A. Element-wise: 5−2=3, 7−3=4, 4−1=3, 9−6=3, giving [[3, 4], [3, 3]].

faq.q: When can two matrices be added in ICSE Class 10?
faq.a: Only when they have exactly the same order — the same number of rows and the same number of columns. You then add the elements that sit in matching positions. A 2×2 can be added to another 2×2, but not to a 2×3.

faq.q: How do you add two 2×2 matrices?
faq.a: Add the corresponding entries one by one: top-left to top-left, top-right to top-right, and so on. If A = [[a, b], [c, d]] and B = [[p, q], [r, s]], then A + B = [[a+p, b+q], [c+r, d+s]].

faq.q: What is the zero matrix and why does it matter for addition?
faq.a: The zero (or null) matrix has every entry equal to 0. It is the additive identity: A + O = A for any matrix A of the same order, just as adding 0 leaves an ordinary number unchanged.

faq.q: Is matrix addition commutative like ordinary addition?
faq.a: Yes. For matrices of the same order, A + B = B + A. This is because each entry is a sum of two numbers, and number addition is commutative. Matrix multiplication, by contrast, is usually not commutative.
